title: Non-custodial trading bot, built with Claude: it trades from your own wallet via a revocable on-chain mandate, no API keys. Looking for the flaws.
author: rushapoil
selftext:
Most bots here (mine included, originally) run on exchange API keys: your funds sit on the exchange, and a third party holds a key that can trade them. The recurring "can a bot drain me / is a trade-only key really safe" worry is baked into that model. I went a different way and wanted to put it in front of this crowd, because you'll actually try to break it.

  
The design:

\- No API keys, no exchange account. The bot trades on-chain, from your own self-custody wallet (MetaMask etc.), on BNB Chain.

\- You sign a capped, revocable on-chain mandate: it can execute swaps within limits you set, and nothing else. It can never withdraw or move your funds out. The chain enforces the ceiling and expiry. You revoke in one transaction.

\- Every fill is a public tx hash. No "trust my screenshot", you can read every trade on-chain.

  
So the whole API-key-risk conversation mostly disappears: there's no key to leak, and worst case you revoke, your funds were never anywhere but your wallet.

  
On the AI part (since this is r/ai_trading): Claude does NOT pick entries. I decided early that asking an LLM for directional edge is a losing game, same conclusion a lot of you reached. The strategy is mechanical and non-predictive: accumulation, buy weakness, scale out into strength, targets fixed at entry. The LLM's only job is regime and sizing, it reads news/macro state and modulates how aggressive the mechanical layer is allowed to be, or pulls it toward zero. AI as a risk dial, not a signal source. That's the part I'd most like this sub to pressure-test.

  
Honesty section, because you rightly demand it: the backtest is about 5.6y of hourly BTC. On a straight bull run a solo instance does NOT beat just holding, and I say so openly. It's not a magic-return machine. What it is: mechanical discipline, self-custody, and on-chain proof, with the AI kept away from the one job it can't do.

  
It's live with real wallets today. I'm not here to pitch, I'm here for the holes:

\- Is a capped/revocable on-chain mandate a meaningfully different risk shape than a trade-only API key, or am I fooling myself?

\- Regime as a modulator vs regime as a filter: better, worse, same?

\- On-chain execution tradeoffs I'm underweighting (gas, MEV, I route through a private mempool but tell me where that leaks)?

  
Tear it apart.
